cases.purpose: Substitute scalars absent from the complete fallback chain as spec 8.3 requires: an Excalifont element and a Liberation Sans (fontFamily 9) element each mix Latin with Linear B U+10000 and U+10001 and the noncharacter U+10FFFF, which no bundled face maps. The official export has no bundled glyph for them and draws whatever the browser's system-font fallback supplies; revision 1 shapes the deterministic basic-Latin ? from Liberation Sans, so the primary face and the replacement face are both exercised, and reports one font.missing-glyph warning per scalar per occurrence in source order. No scalar belongs to the CJK table, so Xiaolai stays out of the fallback chain.

sanitization.reason: Project-authored synthetic scene document; no external content.

exceptions.reason: Spec 8.3's replacement glyph. U+10000, U+10001 and U+10FFFF are absent from every bundled face, so revision 1 shapes each as the deterministic basic-Latin ? from Liberation Sans and reports it as font.missing-glyph (decided on #124). The official export has no glyph for them either and falls through to the pinned container's system fonts: a WenQuanYi Zen Hei placeholder box for U+10000, GNU Unifont Upper's Linear B syllabogram for U+10001, and a blank advance for the uncovered noncharacter U+10FFFF. The divergence is the region from the first unmapped scalar to the end of each of the two lines: that box, glyph and blank against three ? glyphs, and the trailing Latin word the differing advances shift. The leading Latin word on both lines differs only by the sub-pixel glyph-coverage class recorded on #104, #105, #108 and #110.
